chunks: God is the creator of all things, and He is the guarantor of all things.

key_terms.خَالِقُ: Creator, the one who brings something into existence from non-existence
key_terms.وَكِيلٌ: Guarantor, manager, or one who takes care of affairs on behalf of others

ai.seo_question: What does it mean that God is both the Creator and the Guarantor of all things?
ai.summary: This verse from Surah Az-Zumar establishes the foundation of Tawhid by linking Allah's role as the sole Creator (Khaliq) with His continuous management of all affairs (Wakil). In Shia scholarship, this duality underscores the transition from absolute power to divine providence, affirming that creation is not merely an act of origin but an ongoing process sustained by His will.
